# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 8: Frontier AI Just Went on Sale


### Anthropic takes 20% off Claude Fable 5.2, Google adds two more TPU systems with no price tag yet, the Senate moves a bill that sends data centers their own grid bill, and Spotify’s shunt takes 90% off a very small slice.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 11, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/6rg97EkUqEV5NGuABnRcDF) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/dFrZNgvFI7c) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week: Anthropic’s newest frontier model debuts with a 20% price cut. Twenty percent off the frontier. Unless you’re in a hurry. Google rolls out two more systems built on its own AI chips, four this year. Google’s chips have a fashion week now. The Senate moves a permitting bill that would make data centers pay for their own grid upgrades. This bill sends the data center a bill, which means they’ll be sending you a bill. And the Department of Token Efficiency honours a Spotify tool that took about 90% off the tokens on big file reads. Hold your applause until the fine print. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## The tokens


Your agents kept the meter running while you slept.


You’ve been using about


**464 trillion tokens a day** , on


[tokensperday.com](https://tokensperday.com/) ’s live estimate as of 10 November. The site’s last real estimate is a modeled count from 16 July (about 360 trillion a day), grown forward at its own 2.2x-a-year rate. That model adds about


**a trillion tokens a day** , so that’s one more trillion since Monday’s show.


The whole daily total works out to more than


**five billion tokens a second** , by our maths. Faster than anyone in finance can say “Who approved this?”


---


## The landlord’s rate card


Agents need an office, and that’s where our landlords, the clouds, come in.


*“Wipe your feet, darling. The doormat is extra.”*


On the Ornn Compute Price Index, which tracks actual rentals:


-


**NVIDIA H100** settled at


**$3.30 an hour** on the 9 November print, down about


**2%** from the $3.37 we read on Monday’s show. Zoom out and it’s still up about


**16%** over the month, and about


**24%** since 11 August (


[Ornn H100](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/H100%20SXM/index-history) ). Procurement is already putting the 2% in a slide. (Since we recorded, the 10 November print has come in at about $3.10. The landlord is having a sale. Don’t get used to it.)


-


**B200** settled at about


**$9.90 an hour** on the same print, down less than


**1%** on the day. Over the month it’s up about


**33%** , and about


**73%** since 11 August (


[Ornn B200](https://data.ornn.com/api/public-index/gpu/B200/index-history) ).


*“Thirty-three percent in a month? I prefer ’appreciation.’”*


The B200 took the stairs down and the elevator up.


---


## Chips, power and the work


**Chips.** The world has about


**34 million H100-equivalents** , on


[Epoch AI’s chip-sales count](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales) , last updated 21 October. That’s one for about every 250 people on Earth. Please form an orderly queue. It counts chips shipped, not chips switched on. Shipped is not set up. Ask anyone who’s assembled a bookshelf.


**Power.** AI’s data centres draw about


**30 gigawatts** , cooling and all. That’s our estimate, scaled up from


[Epoch’s data-centre tracker](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers) , and it’s holding steady since Friday. For scale,


[Our World in Data’s](https://ourworldindata.org/how-much-energy-do-data-centers-and-artificial-intelligence-use) tally of the IEA’s figures puts AI’s data centres at about


**0.5% of the world’s electricity** in 2025. Counted against all the energy humans use (primary energy, with electricity converted to its fuel equivalent), AI’s share was about


**0.1%** . The planet barely noticed. Your invoice noticed first.


All that to drive a future filled with


**SI: Sale-priced Intelligence** . Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters in Paris on 9 November, “they call it AI, we call it SI” (


[State Department transcript](https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesman/2026/11/secretary-of-state-marco-rubio-remarks-to-the-press-22) ). And so do we.


**The work.** On our bet, sale-priced intelligence is doing about


**11.5% of the hours we work** , about


**40 minutes a day** for everyone who draws a paycheck. Our trend has that share growing about 7% a month, in step with the token count. All three are our estimates. Most of us haven’t improved that fast since college.


The reality check: American workers say AI saves them about


**2%** of their hours, about seven minutes a day by our conversion, in the survey’s latest reading, from July (


[Real-Time Population Survey via FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/RPSGENAITSALL) ). AI saved us seven minutes. We spent them asking whether AI saves us time.


---


## The news: Claude Fable 5.2 goes on sale


Anthropic launched


**Claude Fable 5.2** on Monday. It costs


**$8 per million input tokens** and


**$40 per million output tokens** , down from $10 and $50 for Fable 5.1 (


[Claude pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) ). That’s a


**20%** cut on the top tier. Cheap to get in, pricey to get out. Like an airport parking garage.


Anthropic says the new one is also up to


**30% faster** than Fable 5.1 (


[Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2) ). The bill will keep up. Want it faster still? Fast mode costs double, $16 in and $80 out. Patience is now a pricing tier.


Fable and Mythos 5.2 are the same model; Mythos is only for vetted organizations. Even the model has a dress code.


And Anthropic’s own


**Opus 5.5** still costs half of Fable’s new price, at $4 in and $20 out. The top shelf got cheaper. Per token, the middle shelf is still the deal.


*Per-dollar verdict: cheaper per word, and your agents just found more words.*


---


## The chip aisle that isn’t Nvidia


On Monday, Google added two new systems to the eighth generation of its own AI chips, its TPUs. That’s


**four new TPU systems this year** , which Google says is a first (


[Google](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/infrastructure-and-cloud/global-network/tpu-8i-max-and-8tx/) ). They aren’t new chips: Google repackaged the silicon it launched in April. Same chip, new outfit.


-


**TPU 8i Max** puts two of Google’s inference chips in one package. Google says that’s double the compute, on-chip memory and memory bandwidth, in the same rack space. Two chips, one seat. Tokens get the carpool lane.


-


**TPU 8tx** keeps data protected even while the chip is using it, for regulated companies and governments. Google says it has up to


**2x lower latency** than the TPU 8t, the training chip it’s built on. It’s the only chip in the building that signed an NDA before you did.


Its host processors come from AMD (


[AMD](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1304/amd-epyc-expands-its-leadership-at-the-foundation-of-ai) ). AMD’s stock jumped about


**13%** on Monday, after that news and an


[Oppenheimer upgrade](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/amd-oppenheimer-upgrade-outperform.html) (


[Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/09/stock-market-today-nov-9-amd-jumps-on-oppenheimer-upgrade-and-google-cloud-chip-selection/) ). The doorman had a very good day.


Now, the per-dollar part. Google says April’s TPU 8i gets


**80% better inference price-performance** than the generation before. That’s a math problem, not a coupon. And no eighth-generation TPU is on


[Google’s public price list](https://cloud.google.com/tpu/pricing) yet. Launched, but not priced: the chip version of “let’s circle back.”


The last generation,


[Ironwood](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/infrastructure-and-cloud/google-cloud/ironwood-tpu-age-of-inference/) , lists at


**$12 a chip-hour** on demand in Iowa, or


**$5.40** with a three-year commitment. The cheapest chip-hour is the one you promised three years ago.


Google says nearly


**a hundred customers** now use TPUs, and it has a new tool that plugs into coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor to help move your code onto TPUs. Google built an agent to help your agent switch chips. Somewhere, a sales engineer felt a draft.


*Per-dollar verdict: better per dollar, once there’s a dollar.*


---


## Who pays for the plug


On Monday, the Senate voted


**73 to 25** to move a big permitting bill into debate,


**13 votes** more than the 60 it needed (


[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/senate-infrastructure-bill-data-centers.html) ;


[Utility Dive](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/permitting-bill-advances-in-senate-but-its-future-is-uncertain-after-democ/874250/) ). Seventy-three senators voted the same way. In this Senate, that’s a power surge.


The package would make data centers pay their own way for power and grid upgrades. Senator Shelley Moore Capito’s office says it carries the Ratepayer Protection Act, to make data centers “pay their own way instead of American consumers facing increased costs through rising utility bills” (


[Senate EPW Committee](https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/press-releases-republican?ID=CCD27C16-CBA8-4E56-BFAE-C30D16E0AE61) ). For once, the customer is in the title.


It’s a vote to start debate, not a law, and the House would still have to pass it. The Senate agreed to talk about it. In Washington, that’s a sprint.


*Per-dollar verdict: the grid upgrade lands on the data center, and the data center knows where you live.*


---


## The tier list


How much API value you get for every subscription dollar, on our 10 November run of Adam Holter’s board against real API pricing (the API side is our 27 October snapshot). It ranks value, not usage. It’s the list for people who read nutrition labels.


[Adam Holter @AdamHoltererer Subsidization varies across users and usage patterns Some users get a lot more subsidization than others, but all of them get a ton This could be because the API rates for different types of tokens, such as cached input and output, might be different than the usage rates 10:51 PM · Nov 7, 2026 · 11.8K Views 8 Replies · 2 Reposts · 105 Likes](https://x.com/AdamHoltererer/status/2119201175904149984)


The top ten held their places. Opus and Sonnet tie on three plans, so that’s ten spots on seven lines:


-


**Claude Max** , Opus and Sonnet tied: about


**$77** of API value per plan dollar. Even the landlord doesn’t get terms like that.


-


**Claude Ultra** , Opus and Sonnet tied: about


**$66** .


-


**Claude Pro** , Opus and Sonnet tied: about


**$64** .


-


**Claude Max on Haiku** : about


**$55** .


-


**Google AI Ultra on Gemini Flash** : about


**$49** .


-


**Claude Ultra on Haiku** : about


**$47** .


-


**Claude Pro on Haiku** : about


**$46** (


[Claude pricing](https://claude.com/pricing) ).


The new Fable isn’t on the board yet. On the older Fable 5.1, Claude Max buys about


**$7** of API work per plan dollar. The fanciest model is the worst deal on the plan. Like ordering the tasting menu on a lunch voucher.


And


**Gemini 4 Argon** doubles in price on


**1 December** , from $2 to $4 per million input tokens and $10 to $20 per million output (


[Google AI Studio pricing](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing) ). Just enough time to ignore three reminder emails.


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Somebody out there cut their AI bill. Let’s honor them the only way we know how. (Chainsaw. Watch the video.)


Today’s cost destroyer is a Spotify tool called


**shunt** . It sounds like a plumbing part. Honestly, that’s the job.


Spotify principal product manager Dimitri Mazmanov wrote it up: big file reads go to a cheaper model, which sends back a summary (


[Spotify Engineering](https://engineering.atspotify.com/2026/09/portal-by-spotify-cut-my-claude-code-token-usage-by-90) ). Delegation. The most human thing an AI has ever done. On his own tests, it cut the tokens on those reads by about


**90%** (82% to 94% across three benchmarks, per the


[README](https://github.com/spotify/portal-ai-plugins/blob/main/plugins/shunt/README.md) ). Spotify mostly skips songs. Now it skips tokens.


Then developer


**Jason MacLulich** replayed four weeks of his own Claude Code work: about


**$10,000** at list API prices (


[MacLulich](https://maclulich.com/blog/spotify-90-percent-claude-code/) ). For one developer. That’s a hire, billed by the token.


-


The tool only catches big file reads. For him, those were just under


**1%** of his spend.


-


At most, it would save him about


**0.8%** , before paying for the cheaper model. Ninety percent off almost nothing is still almost nothing.


-


Those reads averaged about


**12 cents** each; the tool saves about


**11 cents** a read. Don’t spend it all on one prompt.


-


Most of his bill was context getting carried around. Cache reads alone were about


**half** (53%).


Somebody’s been hoarding context. (The goblin would like a word. Watch the video.)


**The fine print:** Spotify’s 90% is one product manager’s own test, not Spotify’s bill. The cheaper model missed a subtle thread-safety bug. And you need Spotify’s Portal to run it. Batteries, and Spotify, not included. Ask your CFO if shunt is right for you.


A good tool, if your bill is mostly file reads. Check the slice before you cheer the percent.


Still: chainsaw approved.


**Bonus round.** Simon Willison spotted a tip in Anthropic’s new prompting guide for Fable 5.2: tell it, “This codebase is yours.”


[Simon Willison @simonw](https://x.com/simonw/status/2120029347948220500)[When Anthropic release a new model it's always worth taking a look at their updated prompting guide - here's an entertaining tip to make Fable 5.2 less likely to be cautious in how it improves existing code: tell it "This codebase is yours"](https://x.com/simonw/status/2120029347948220500)[platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-…](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2#say-who-owns-the-code)


5:42 AM · Nov 10, 2026


·


306K Views

390 Replies

4.24K Likes


In Anthropic’s tests on small coding tasks, Fable merged repeated code in about


**half** the tries with that sentence, and in


**under a tenth** without it (


[Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 prompting guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompting-claude-fable-5-2#say-who-owns-the-code) ). Managers have said that for decades. First time anyone believed it. The catch: about


**1.5 times** the output tokens, and changes nobody asked for. In one try in six to ten, Fable changed how an existing feature works. Give it the keys, and it knocks out a wall. Check the diff.


So judge it by cost per useful change, not cost per turn. If it saves you the cleanup round, the extra tokens pay their way. Tell your agent it owns the code. Keep the company card in your name.


**Second bonus.** Theo, of t3.gg, has a trick for agents that keep hitting usage limits: get Anthropic’s


**$100** Claude Max plan, install


[T3 Code](https://t3.codes/) , and tell your agent to route work through it to Opus 5.5 for any task where it fits.


[Theo - t3.gg @theo If you're running into usage limits with Grok Bot (I know I have been), try this: 1. Sign up for $100 Claude plan 2. Install T3 Code 3. Do this 4. Tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable" Should help a lot! Theo - t3.gg @theo Overhauled the flow for controlling T3 Code from other devices :) You can now cmd+k "mcp" to set up the connector for whatever agents you want to control T3 Code from :) 3:24 AM · Nov 10, 2026 · 123K Views 159 Replies · 46 Reposts · 1.7K Likes](https://x.com/theo/status/2119994608516276256)


Your agent found the one coworker on salary. The catch: Max has its own usage limits, every five hours and every week, set at


**five times** the Pro plan’s (


[Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11049741-what-is-the-max-plan) ). You didn’t escape the limit. You upgraded it. Theo didn’t give a savings number, so we won’t either. Full disclosure: T3 Code is his company’s app.


A flat rate is just a meter that hasn’t met your agent yet.
